'''''Berberis napaulensis''''' (syn. ''B. duclouxiana'';<ref name="POWO1"/> {{langx|ne|जमाने मान्द्रो}}, {{langx|zh|尼泊尔十大功劳}}) is a shrub in the family [[Berberidaceae]] described as a species in 1821. It is native to the [[Himalayas]] (northwestern [[India]], [[Nepal]], [[Bhutan]], [[Sikkim]], [[Assam]]), and into the mountains of southwestern [[China]] ([[Tibet]], [[Yunnan]], [[Guangxi]], and [[Sichuan]]), [[Myanmar]], [[Thailand]], and [[Vietnam]], growing at altitudes of 1,200-3,000 metres.<ref name="POWO"/><ref name="efloras">[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200008401 Flora of China: ''Mahonia napaulensis'' Candolle]</ref><ref name="efloras duclouxiana">[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200008391 Flora of China: ''Mahonia duclouxiana'']</ref> This species is used medicinally throughout the Sikkim Eastern Himalayas.<ref name="O'Neill_al2017">{{cite journal |last1=O'Neill |first1=A. R.|last2=Badola |first2=H.K. |last3=Dhyani |first3=P. P. |last4=Rana |first4=S. K. |date=2017 |title=Integrating ethnobiological knowledge into biodiversity conservation in the Eastern Himalayas |journal=Journal of Ethnobiology and Ethnomedicine |volume=13 |issue=1 |pages=21 |doi=10.1186/s13002-017-0148-9 |pmid=28356115 |pmc=5372287 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Mahonia duclouxiana - San Francisco Botanical Garden - DSC09805.JPG|thumb|left|Labeled as ''Mahonia duclouxiana'' - San Francisco Botanical Garden]]
''Berberis napaulensis'' is an evergreen shrub (rarely a small tree) that grows to 1–7 metres tall. The leaves are 17–70 centimetres long and 7–22 cm broad, with 4-12 pairs of leaflets plus a larger terminal leaflet, all shiny above, yellowish-green below, and with spined margins. The flowers are yellow, borne in large [[panicle]]s. The berries are spherical, deep purple, 5–8 millimetres in diameter.<ref name="efloras" /><ref name="efloras duclouxiana"/>

==Taxonomy==
''Berberis napaulensis'' was initially scientifically named and described by [[Augustin Pyramus de Candolle]] as ''Mahonia napaulensis'' in 1821.<ref name="POWO">{{cite POWO |id=60461528-2 |title=''Berberis napaulensis'' (DC.) Spreng. |access-date=14 November 2023}}</ref><ref>Candolle, Augustin Pyramus de. 1821. Regni Vegetabilis Systema Naturale 2: 21</ref> As part of a long running debate between botanists on whether ''[[Mahonia]]'' should be a [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] of ''[[Berberis]]'', [[Kurt Polycarp Joachim Sprengel]] classified it as ''Berberis napaulensis'' in 1825.<ref name="POWO" /> A paper published by [[Joseph Edward Laferrière]] in 1997 gave arguments in favour of ''Berberis'' as the correct classification,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Laferrière |first1=Joseph Edward |title=Transfer of Specific and Infraspecific Taxa from ''Mahonia'' to ''Berberis'' (Berberidaceae) |journal=Botanicheskii Zhurnal |date=1997 |volume=82 |issue=9 |pages=95–98 |url=http://en.arch.botjournal.ru/?t=issues&id=19970909&rid=pdf_0005055 |access-date=8 November 2023 |archive-date=7 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231107012402/http://en.arch.botjournal.ru/?t=issues&id=19970909&rid=pdf_0005055 |url-status=dead }}</ref> while Yu & Chung (2017) recommended acceptance of four genera including ''Mahonia'' as distinct.<ref name="v581">{{cite journal |last1=Yu |first1=Chih-Chieh |last2=Chung |first2=Kuo-Fang |title=Why ''Mahonia''? Molecular recircumscription of ''Berberis'' s.l., with the description of two new genera, ''Alloberberis'' and ''Moranothamnus'' |journal=TAXON |volume=66 |issue=6 |date=2017 |issn=0040-0262 |doi=10.12705/666.6 |pages=1371–1392 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.12705/666.6 |access-date=2026-09-12}}</ref> As of 2023, the ''[[Plants of the World Online]]'' database (POWO) follows Laferrière's single-genus classification.<ref name="POWO" /> The [[Flora of China (series)|''Flora of China'']] treats the species in ''Mahonia'';<ref name="efloras"/> it also treats ''Berberis duclouxiana'' as a separate species, as ''Mahonia duclouxiana''.<ref name="efloras duclouxiana"/>

==Ecology==
In [[Chiang Mai Province]], Thailand, a species of [[rust fungus]] ''Pucciniosira cornuta'' (synonym of ''[[Gambleola cornuta]]'' {{Au|Massee (1898)}}) infects ''Berberis nepalensis''.<ref>{{cite conference <!-- Citation bot no -->|last1=Ono |first1=Yoshitaka |last2=Okane |first2=Izumi |last3=Unartngam |first3=Jintana |last4=Ayawong |first4=Chanjira |chapter=Pucciniosira cornuta found on Berberis nepaulensis in Thailand. |title=Rust flora of East and Southeast Asia. |journal=Japanese Journal of Mycology |date=May 2021 |volume=62 |issue=1 |pages=31–34 |doi=10.18962/jjom.jjom.R02-16}}</ref>
